source_assessment: The source is a genuine undirected RKD paper extract covering the full method: distance-wise (pairwise Euclidean) and angle-wise (triplet cosine) relational distillation losses, mini-batch tuple sampling, Huber loss, and distance normalization. Pages 1 and 5 are sampled, so implementation details outside those (e.g., exact hyperparameter ranges, full multi-task recipe, full metric-learning/batch-construction specifics) are only partially covered. The extract is sufficient to justify relational-loss components, but directional/paired and causal/temporal twists are analogies, not statements from the source.

ideas.title: Directed relative-distance distillation on causally valid pairs
ideas.source_component_and_location: From SOURCE.txt Section 3.2.1: distance-wise potential psi_D = ||t_i - t_j||^2 and its distance-normalized formulation; Section 3.2.4 notes RKD works best on embedding-like outputs rather than softmax outputs.
ideas.task_mapping: Predicted teacher/student representation vectors for paired rows can be treated as embedding-like features; distillation targets relative distances between paired representations rather than absolute feature values.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a small auxiliary loss that penalizes differences in the teacher versus student relative distance structure across valid pairs, using a normalized squared-distance potential analogous to RKD-D but restricted to causally valid pairs and optionally re-weighted by clip-weight magnitude.
ideas.assumptions: Teacher and student representations can be defined for each row; there exists a sensible pairing rule consistent with causal/ temporal constraints; the representation space behaves enough like a metric space that relative distances carry useful signal.
ideas.predicted_observable: Student may track teacher-relative structure better on causally admissible pairs than on unconstrained pairs; effect should be largest where absolute feature matching is weak but relational structure is stable.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Train a small student with and without the directed relational loss on a local causal-screened subset, comparing pair-relation matching and final utility on rows satisfying need_prediction and is_scored.
ideas.matched_control: Same student and teacher, same pairs, but with pointwise feature-matching distillation instead of relational distillation.
ideas.falsifier: If relational loss helps no more than pointwise matching on the same valid pairs, then the benefit is not from relational transfer in this setting.
ideas.resource_estimate: Small; pair construction and pairwise losses are cheap on a limited subset, compatible with a cheap local test.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Add as a small auxiliary term on top of the existing recurrent blend's training/adaptation path, not as a replacement for the main predictor.
ideas.genuinely_new_part: Directed/paired relational distillation with causal-pair screening, rather than all-pair minibatch tuples from an image retrieval minibatch.
ideas.possible_interactions: May interact with sequence reset, warmup filtering, and clipping; could also interact with any representation normalization used in the teacher/student pipeline.

ideas.title: Angle-wise relational distillation over triplets anchored by a driver feature
ideas.source_component_and_location: From SOURCE.txt Section 3.2.2: angle-wise potential psi_A as cosine of the angle formed by three embedding vectors, with Huber loss; Section 3.2.4 notes angle-wise can give more flexibility.
ideas.task_mapping: For triples of rows, the relational signal is the angle among their teacher/student feature vectors; anchoring by a shared driver or common regime may make the triplet relation more meaningful.
ideas.proposed_change: Introduce a light angle-wise distillation term computed on a constrained triplet family, for example anchor-positive-contrastive triples defined by a chosen shared feature or regime signal, transferring teacher angles to the student.
ideas.assumptions: Triplet relations among rows are defined and not dominated by noise; an anchoring rule produces sufficiently informative triples; student representation space supports meaningful angles.
ideas.predicted_observable: Angular structure alignment may improve for triplets sharing a driver even when pairwise distance alignment is similar; may be most useful when the task involves contrastive regime separation.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Compare student with small angle-wise distillation on driver-anchored triples versus no relational term, using local validation on scored rows.
ideas.matched_control: Same architecture and training, but with distance-wise relational term or pointwise distillation at comparable weight.
ideas.falsifier: If driver-anchored angular distillation does not improve pair/triplet relational alignment or downstream scoring beyond controls, then third-order angles are not useful here.
ideas.resource_estimate: Low to moderate; triplets increase tuple count but can be limited by anchoring and sampling.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Explore as an optional relational add-on, likely after a stable base student is available.
ideas.genuinely_new_part: Choosing the tuple family by causal/ shared-driver anchoring instead of exhaustive minibatch triplets.
ideas.possible_interactions: May interact with normalization, clipping, and any feature groups used for pairing; angle sensitivity may depend on representation scale.

ideas.title: Temporal relational contrast across consecutive valid rows
ideas.source_component_and_location: From SOURCE.txt Section 3.2 and Figure 2 concept: transfer relational potential between teacher and student rather than point-wise outputs; Section 3.2.1 distance potential is the concrete building block used here as an analogy.
ideas.task_mapping: If rows are processed in order and state resets between sequences, then relational change across adjacent valid rows within a sequence can be treated as a distillation target structure.
ideas.proposed_change: Define a temporal relational term that compares teacher and student differences or relative positions between consecutive causally valid rows, encouraging the student to reproduce the teacher's short-horizon relational dynamics.
ideas.assumptions: Short-horizon relational changes within a sequence are informative and approximately stationary enough to transfer; temporal adjacency is compatible with the causal/ screening constraints.
ideas.predicted_observable: Student may capture local temporal relational patterns more faithfully, especially where pointwise targets are weak but transitions are structured.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Ablate temporal relational term versus same-weight static relational term on local sequences with reset, measuring whether temporal relations improve on scored rows.
ideas.matched_control: Same student with a static relational loss using the same rows but ignoring adjacency.
ideas.falsifier: If temporal adjacency adds no benefit beyond static relational matching from the same rows, then the temporal relation is not transferring useful knowledge.
ideas.resource_estimate: Cheap; only needs adjacent valid pairs within sequences.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Try as a targeted temporal regularizer if sequence order matters and a recurrent state is used locally.
ideas.genuinely_new_part: Using consecutive-row relational change as the transferred object rather than unordered tuples.
ideas.possible_interactions: Could interact with warmup, reset policy, sequence boundaries, and any hidden state carried across rows.

ideas.title: Causal-robustness relational distillation with paired view perturbation
ideas.mechanism_family: relational distillation with invariance / re-encoded views
ideas.source_component_and_location: From SOURCE.txt Sections 3.2.1-3.2.4: relational potential and distillation loss framework; especially the property that RKD transfers structure and can be combined with other losses, plus the general idea of transferring relations rather than absolute outputs.
ideas.task_mapping: If two causal views of the same underlying row/ situation can be formed within the allowed feature set, then relational invariance across those views is a candidate transferable structure.
ideas.proposed_change: Construct paired views from within the causal feature set where permissible, then add a relational term encouraging the student to preserve teacher-like relations across views, effectively distilling relational invariance rather than raw predictions.
ideas.assumptions: Valid paired views exist under causal and feature-access constraints; relational invariance across those views carries signal; the teacher encodes some stable relational structure worth transferring.
ideas.predicted_observable: Student may become more stable across admissible perturbations without using disallowed future or identity information; relational stability may improve on scored rows if perturbation structure is meaningful.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Compare student with view-invariant relational term to student without it, on a local perturbation-consistent validation split that respects causal constraints.
ideas.matched_control: Same student trained with pointwise view-matching or with no view term.
ideas.falsifier: If relational invariance across views does not improve stability or scoring beyond pointwise view matching, then relational invariance is not the effective ingredient.
ideas.resource_estimate: Low; requires constructing allowable paired views and relational comparisons.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Position as a robustness-oriented auxiliary loss, not as the main forecasting signal.
ideas.genuinely_new_part: Re-encoding paired causal views and distilling relational invariance across them, rather than transferring static minibatch relations.
ideas.possible_interactions: May interact with feature-group definition, perturbation choice, clip normalization, and scoring weighting.

ideas.title: Unconventional: teacher-relation amortization as an unsupervised student regularizer
ideas.source_component_and_location: From SOURCE.txt Section 3.2 and Section 4: RKD can train from teacher relations even without the original task loss in some settings, and relational losses can complement other objectives; the relational framework is the main transferable idea.
ideas.task_mapping: Treat the teacher's relational structure as a weak supervisory signal for the student's representation geometry, using a small relational regularizer independent of immediate label availability on a subset of rows.
ideas.proposed_change: Add a small relational regularizer that encourages the student to preserve teacher-like relations on a deliberately chosen subset of rows, even when task labels are not used for that term, to shape representation structure before or alongside the main task objective.
ideas.assumptions: Teacher relations contain structure usable as a regularizer; a subset of rows can be used without violating causal/ screening constraints; the regularizer is light enough not to dominate the task objective.
ideas.predicted_observable: Student representation geometry may become more teacher-like and possibly more organized, with unclear direct effect on final pooled correlation; benefit is qualitative and setting-dependent.
ideas.cheapest_discriminating_test: Add and remove the relational regularizer in a small local run, checking representation-structure metrics and any change on scored rows.
ideas.matched_control: Same student and training budget without the relational regularizer.
ideas.falsifier: If the relational regularizer does not change student geometry or scored-row behavior relative to control, then the unsupervised relational signal is not useful here.
ideas.resource_estimate: Cheap to moderate; depends on subset size and tuple sampling.
ideas.suggested_parent_direction: Try only if representation geometry seems underconstrained; otherwise do not prioritize.
ideas.genuinely_new_part: Using teacher relational structure primarily as an unsupervised regularizer rather than as a direct distillation target tied to the main loss.
ideas.possible_interactions: Could interact with main task weighting, regularization strength, and any representation normalization.
